thisPc.copyTitle: Copy to a USB drive or NAS
thisPc.copyHint: Every new backup is also copied to this folder, so the data survives if this PC breaks or is stolen. Anyone who can open the folder can read the backups.
thisPc.copyNone: No folder chosen: backups are kept on this PC only.
thisPc.copyNasHint: A NAS folder must let this PC write without a user name and password.
thisPc.publicNetwork: Windows treats {{networks}} as a Public network, so office PCs cannot connect. Switch it to Private if this is your shop's own network.
thisPc.fixedIpHint: Office PCs find this PC again by themselves if its address changes. With a router, reserving a fixed address for this PC (DHCP reservation) avoids even the short wait.

corrections.title: Cancel or reverse
corrections.cancelHint: For a mistake in an open period: it is taken out of the books and the stock as if it never happened, and its number is freed for the next document.
corrections.reverseHint: When the period is closed or the supplier already has it: a reversal with its own number, dated on the day you choose.
corrections.reissueOf: Reissued with the number of the cancelled

errors.document_has_dependants: Later documents follow this one: undo {{documents}} first.
errors.cancel_period_locked: Its period is locked, so it cannot be cancelled: reverse it instead.
errors.cancel_only: This document has nothing in the books to reverse: cancel it instead.
errors.document_is_a_reversal: A reversal cannot itself be cancelled or reversed.
errors.document_not_posted: Only a posted document can be cancelled or reversed.
errors.invalid_reversal: A reversal cannot be dated before the document.
errors.recost_into_locked_period: A later stock movement is in a locked period, so this cannot be done.
errors.permission_denied: You don't have permission to do that.

corrections.wasSent: This document was printed or sent to the customer: they hold its number. Cancelling frees it for reuse; reversing keeps it and writes a dated reversal, which is usually better once the customer has it.

pdc.memoNote: Post-dated cheques are a memo: nothing is in the books until the bank clears them.
pdc.bankHint: The bank the cheque is drawn on
pdc.drawnOn: Our bank account it is drawn on
pdc.intendedHint: Settled when the cheque clears, as far as they are still open; the rest becomes an advance.
pdc.noOpenBills: No open bills: the whole cheque becomes an advance when it clears.

deposit.received: Still nothing in the books until the bank clears it.

clear.received: Posts a receipt on this date and settles the bills it was for.
clear.issued: Posts a payment on this date and settles the bills it was for.

bounce.received: Nothing is posted: the customer still owes the bills. A bank charge, if any, is posted as an expense.
bounce.issued: Nothing is posted: the supplier is still owed. A bank charge, if any, is posted as an expense.

return.received: The cheque goes back to the customer unused.

cancel.issued: The cheque is void; nothing was posted.
